topic: The overall status of Slavic mythology

positions.name: attested
positions.description: The 980 'destruction of the idols' and the Kiev idol list (Perun, Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Veles, Mokosh) are attested in the Primary Chronicle

positions.name: reconstructed
positions.description: The genealogies (Svarog-Veles, Nebo-Perun), the 'Perun-Veles' conflict, the seasonal cycle, and the cosmology are scholarly reconstructions

how_we_present_it: We mark every claim with its evidence_status (attested / attested(folk) / reconstructed / variant / modern). We do NOT present reconstructions as if they were attested myths.

positions.name: S6
positions.description: A scholarly reconstruction (Ivanov & Toporov) of an Indo-European 'sky-father vs. underworld-serpent' duality, not a single attested Slavic myth

how_we_present_it: We present it explicitly as a reconstruction, not as an attested myth.

positions.name: reconstructed
positions.description: The 'sky-father', the supreme deity in folk belief

positions.name: debated
positions.description: Whether a formal pre-Christian god or a folk Christianization that absorbed Perun's role

how_we_present_it: We present Nebo as the reconstructed supreme sky-father, noting the debate.

positions.name: folk
positions.description: The 'Kupala' night is a well-attested folk fire-and-water festival

positions.name: debated
positions.description: Whether Jarilo is the 'Kupala' god or the 'Kupala' is a separate older ritual

how_we_present_it: We present the 'Kupala' as well-attested folk ritual; the Jarilo connection as debated.

positions.name: folk
positions.description: The 'drowning of Marzanna' is a well-attested folk spring-ritual

positions.name: debated
positions.description: Whether Morana was a formal pre-Christian goddess or a folk death/winter figure

how_we_present_it: We present the ritual as well-attested; the goddess's pre-Christian status as debated.

positions.name: attested
positions.description: The 980 'destruction of the idols' is the oldest attested event

positions.name: reconstructed
positions.description: The pre-Christian religion is c. 6th-10th c. (reconstructed); the surviving texts are c. 1113 CE and later

how_we_present_it: We make clear that the religion is much older than the surviving texts.
